patterns: Election-night volume dominated: 86 hits (~6.4M views, 4.0% likes) mention voting, ballots or polls; 41 House/Senate-control hits pulled ~5.2M, led by Gunther's 'autopsy should start in the Senate' (~464k at 4.0%) and rawsalerts' Polymarket 'Democrats seize both chambers' (~344k at 1.2%)

Blame-the-leader posts earned the most love: 13 John Thune hits drew ~2.36M views at 8.3% likes, including 'needs to be removed from Senate Leadership' (~234k at 15.5%), 'COWARD' (~270k at 13.0%) and 'failed to deliver' (~415k at 10.1%)

Texas was the top battleground story: 32 Texas hits (~3.6M at 2.7%), led by Ted Cruz's 'Democrats could well win every statewide position' (~873k at 0.6%) and 'If Texas turns blue' (~722k at 1.5%); 'socialism' fear framing added ~894k at 4.5%
Shock clip with low love: alx's Galloway-calls-for-Musk-execution post was the window's #1 (~952k at 0.15%), outrage reach with almost no likes
Bright-spot wins and election-security claims had the highest like rates: Hageman/Wyoming ~406k at 11.0%, Anna Paulina Luna holds FL-13 (~144k at 15.6%), and 9 cheat/fraud/security posts at 11.2%
Keywords: Thune, Texas, House, Senate, Polymarket, socialism, Talarico, El-Sayed, Ohio/Husted, autopsy, veto, Wyoming
virals_narrative: The outsider AI sweep (last ~48h, three searches, ~75 posts) was thin again. The biggest item was @BoringBiz_ on Goldman Sachs pushing AI to ~46,000 employees (~149k views), followed by @mark_k's 'November could be a HUGE month for AI model releases' list (~33k) and Manning's 'calling an LLM doesn't make your software an AI agent' (~5k). Smaller threads: Yahoo News on OpenAI and Anthropic election 'war rooms', OpenAI appointing former Army secretary Dan Driscoll, Anthropic's quarter revenue/cost talk, and NVIDIA app AI-agent settings. Much of the rest was '120 AI tools' list spam.
narrative_synthesis: Election-night window (Tue ~11:13 ET to Wed ~11:07 ET): 253 hits and ~18.5M views from 253 originals, every one over 5k. The story arc moved from the Texas/Michigan/Ohio get-out-the-vote push to results posts saying Democrats took the House and Senate, then to a blame wave aimed at John Thune that earned the highest like rates. The single biggest post was off-topic outrage (Galloway/Musk clip, ~952k at 0.15%). For @patriotpunishr0, the openings are useful next-step posts: what the flip actually changes and when, checking full clips before sharing, waiting for the final count, and turning anger into a call to your senator.
